label: aival3-n1
_why: THE QUADRATIC ai_value LADDER, ONE FULL-CENTURY RUN (user-ruled 2026-08-20: 'make it 1000*(era+1)^2 then', 'and run n=1'). ai_value = 1000 x (era+1)^2 on every tier: e0 1000 / e1 4000 / e2 9000 / e3 16000 / e4 25000 / e5 36000. ARM: {kind: config, config: config/mod_config.aival3.json} - a full modded build, no overlay, no control. SPAN 1836.1.1 -> 1936.1.1, n=1, metrics identical to aival2-n2, aival-n4, canon-n7 and the pinned vanilla baseline.
_the_ladder_and_what_changed: ⭐ THIS IS THE FIRST REAL STEEPENING. Both previous arms were 1:6 rung-to-rung (500 x (era+1) and 1000 x (era+1)); this is 1:36. F76 established the frame that matters: ai_value is scored against EVERY building the AI considers, and 75 vanilla buildings carry no ai_value at all and therefore sit at the ENGINE DEFAULT 1000 - every farm, plantation, ranch, logging camp, oil rig, fishery, and the base light/heavy industry buildings. So the meaningful column is each rung's ratio TO THAT FIELD: e0 1x / e1 4x / e2 9x / e3 16x / e4 25x / e5 36x, against aival2's 1x/2x/3x/4x/5x/6x. The top rung goes from 6x the field to 36x. ⚠ SCALE CHECK: 36000 sits above every vanilla monument (10000) but below the skyscraper (50000) and the canals (100000), so it stays inside the range vanilla itself uses - this is not off the end of the scale. ⚠ e0 is UNCHANGED at 1000, level with the field, exactly as in aival2: this ladder does not penalise the oldest rung further, it only lifts the newer ones.
_the_new_distortion_to_watch: ⚠⚠ REGISTERED BEFORE THE RUN, because this ladder introduces it and the previous two did not. The ladder is keyed to ERA, not to rung position, so an industry whose chain STOPS EARLY can never reach the high values. Tops reachable per industry: shipyard 4000 (its ladder ends at e1); food, textile, furniture, port, railway 25000; the other sixteen 36000. Under aival2's 1:6 shipyard's best rung was 1/3 of a field-leader's best; here it is 1/9. THE PREDICTION: shipyard should lose construction share, and the five 25000-capped industries should lose a little to the 36000 ones. If that happens it is NOT a bug in the ladder, it is what an era-keyed ladder means for a chain that ends early - but it must be measured rather than discovered later, and it is the most likely place for the first genuine OVERSHOOT to appear inside the tiered sector.

THE ARM IS THE CANONICAL CONFIG PLUS ONE FIELD: derived from config/mod_config.json at git 636758f with a clean tree (sha256 D9512C19AEB7AA0ACC1E67D830269BA60BA0910EB17DE6AAD66D4E96D82238EB, byte-identical to canon-n7's frozen copy). A structural diff reports 105 differences and ALL 105 are industries[].tiers[].ai_value, verified by explicit path test. ⚠ 105, not the 104 of the two previous arms: tooling's e3 rung was 2000 in the canonical config and 500 x (3+1) is also 2000, so it did not move under aival; 1000 x 4^2 = 16000 does. building_ai_value untouched (trade_center 5000). aival3's sha256 is DAD3D735A86C298D851A51AC0E41E7939DAA1C6DADA244CA45BAA378B72168C0. THE FREEZE IS LANDMINE L10; no build-path file (build.ps1, preflight.ps1, telemetry_lib.ps1, emit_techs.mjs, emit_research_events.mjs, convert_history.ps1, extract_start.ps1) may be touched for the duration. NO CONTROL ARM, by standing user ruling.
_the_seven_that_do_not_get_it: As in both previous arms: 98 of 105 tiers emit the ladder. power (3) and railway (4) are clone_from_vanilla and keep their complex conditional vanilla ai_value blocks (user ruling 2026-08-19). ⭐ THAT MAKES THEM THE CONTROL, and it is far more informative at this setting than at the last: their vanilla base values are 1000 (power) and 2000 (railway) against a tiered field now running 1000-36000, so they are now an order of magnitude behind everything around them. A large fall in power/railway construction is the EXPECTED consequence of the ruling, not evidence about the lever; a fall in something that DID get the ladder is.
_comparison: PRIMARY: against aival2-n2 (20260820_095104, n=2) and aival-n4 (20260819_215528, n=4) - all three are 1.13.11 on this machine, so the three-point ladder curve is a clean same-patch series. Below-best share so far: canon-n7 52.94% (sd 3.17pp, n=6) -> aival 50.52% (sd 0.81, n=4) -> aival2 47.17% (sd 0.60, n=2). SECONDARY: canon-n7 as the no-ladder baseline and the pinned vanilla baseline 20260813_083557:vanilla for the G5 panels, both 1.13.10, both with the patch caveat. ⚠⚠ n=1. The measured per-run sd of the headline metric is 0.60-0.81pp inside a 1.13.11 arm, so a SINGLE run resolves a ~3pp move comfortably and resolves nothing under ~1.5pp. It cannot speak to variance at all, and it cannot be quoted with a spread. Read it as ONE POINT ON A CURVE whose other three points have n=6/4/2 - that is what makes n=1 defensible here and would not make it defensible for a standalone claim.
_watch: (1) THE HEADLINE: below-best share against the 52.94 / 50.52 / 47.17 series. F76's mechanism predicts a further fall, and this is the test of whether it keeps paying or saturates. (2) ⭐ THE OVERSHOOT, finally likely: extraction and agriculture carry NO ai_value change and now compete against rungs worth up to 36000. aival2 read extraction 1.00x and agriculture 0.93x; if the raw sector is ever going to be starved it is here. Read absolute lv/run beside share - a share fall with flat absolute is manufacturing growing, not agriculture dying. (3) THE EARLY-STOPPING CHAINS, per _the_new_distortion_to_watch: shipyard (caps at 4000) and the five 25000-capped industries. (4) THE ERA MIX of construction: aival2 moved e4 to 1.70x and e5 to 2.80x while e0 held flat at 1.03x. Does e0 finally fall in ABSOLUTE terms, or does the whole tiered sector just grow again? (5) THE TWO G5 PANELS (advanced_panel.mjs, tiered_panel.mjs), pooled GBR/USA/FRA/NET/BEL/PRU/GER: aival2 was the first arm with pooled GDP ABOVE vanilla (1.045x) on 0.923x the productive workers at 1.190x output per worker. ⚠ tiered_panel's productivity still has NO vanilla denominator until the 2026-08-22/23 v6 vanilla runs. (6) RESEARCH EVENTS as distinct (stage, tech, country) triples (L23) - 5,264/78 at aival2, 5,113/79 at aival, 5,411/76 at canon-n7. The bars feed on predecessor-tier EMPLOYMENT, so a ladder that finally suppresses e0 in absolute terms should show here first, and this is the first setting likely to do it.
_cost: 1 run x 100 in-game years. Recent runs on this machine and patch: 2.49-2.77 h. So ~2h45 plus one build of ~8s and the concurrent save harvest. ~0.2 GB of retained session.
_caveats: ⚠⚠ n=1: no spread, no variance statement, and no standalone claim. Defensible only as the fourth point of a same-patch curve whose other points carry n=6/4/2. THE PATCH CONFOUND IS ABSENT for the primary comparison (aival, aival2 and this are all 1.13.11 on this machine) and PRESENT for canon-n7 and the vanilla baseline, both 1.13.10. ROW P: machine must stay idle, and NO ANALYSIS RUNS WHILE THE GAME RUNS (aival-n4 lost a clean timing row to that; its MACHINE_LOAD.md records both the episode and its own withdrawal). building_inventory DELIBERATELY ABSENT (boot burst overflows the shared log ring, L4/L9). Save harvest ON and concurrent - required, every panel reads the yearly summaries. moderate_consolidation, verified from world.game_rules not from intent. L17: preflight.ps1 -Session post-run. L19: no orphaned victoria3.exe at launch.
